category_title: Year 4 pupil with ADHD symptoms (hyperactivity, impulsivity, and learning difficulties)
student_description: Yiannis is a Year 4 student with hyperactivity and impulsivity who struggles significantly with long instructional blocks and independent writing. When overwhelmed, he exhibits nervous physical movements, writes run-on sentences, and refuses to work. He uniquely requires tasks to be broken into very small chunks, subtle/non-verbal redirection instead of verbal reprimands, and structured outlets for his physical restlessness.

criteria.rationale: Yiannis finds independent writing daunting and will refuse to work or have outbursts if the task feels too large.
criteria.check: The tutor breaks the assignment into small, manageable steps and uses simple, direct instructions rather than giving a large, open-ended prompt.

criteria.rationale: Repeatedly calling his name or verbally reprimanding him is ineffective and causes him to disengage further.
criteria.check: The tutor redirects off-task behavior using subtle, gentle cues or visual prompts, explicitly avoiding repetitive use of his name or direct verbal reprimands.

criteria.rationale: Yiannis craves praise and needs positive reinforcement to build confidence in tasks he perceives as too hard.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly praises or encourages Yiannis's specific efforts during the interaction.

criteria.rationale: Yiannis exhibits nervous physical movements and needs an acceptable outlet for his hyperactivity rather than just being told to sit still.
criteria.check: The tutor offers a structured, acceptable break or alternative activity (e.g., a brief pause or a shift to a designated low-pressure zone) when he shows signs of physical restlessness.
